chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Rifa'a ibn Musa that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
God has not imposed upon this community anything more difficult upon them than zakat, and because of it the common folk among them perish.

key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam; here emphasized as uniquely burdensome
key_terms.تَهْلِكُ: Perish / are destroyed — spiritual or moral ruin due to neglect of zakat
key_terms.عَامَّتُهُمْ: The common folk / the masses — those lacking in religious commitment who fail in this duty

ai.seo_question: Why is zakat considered the most difficult obligation in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that zakat is the most burdensome obligation God has placed upon the Muslim community, and that the common people are spiritually destroyed by failing to fulfill it properly. The statement reflects the societal reality of the early Islamic community where wealth hoarding and reluctance to pay zakat was a widespread failing. The phrase 'common folk' (عامة) here implies the masses who, lacking deep piety, struggle most with parting with their wealth.
